figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. Phylogenetic relationship among enfumafungin terpene cyclase (efuA), other squalene-hopene cyclases (SHC) and lanosterol synthases
(LS) as inferred from the respective protein sequences. Maximum likelihood (ML) bootstrap support values above 50%, from 100 RAxML repli-
cates are assigned to the nodes of the tree topology of the most likely tree found by RAxML. GenBank accession numbers are followed by spe-
cies names. EfuA is highlighted in red, the putative polytolypin synthase in blue and the H. carpetanum LS in green. TC-GT, terpene cyclase/
glycosyltransferase fusion proteins. [Colour ﬁgure can be viewed at wileyonlinelibrary.com]

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Phylogenetic relationship of enfumafungin glycosyltransferase and its closest BLAST hits as inferred from the respective protein
sequences. Likelihood (ML) bootstrap support values above 50%, from 100 RAxML replicates are assigned to the nodes of the tree topology of
the most likely tree found by RAxML. GenBank accession numbers are followed by species names.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Alignment of related terpene cyclase-glycosyl transferase fusion protein sequences. Homologies are colour-coded based on polarity
(red—acidic aa, blue—basic aa, green—polar, yellow—nonpolar). The terpene cyclase domain is highlighted in red and the glycosyl transferase
domain in blue. The black box indicates the conserved DXDD active site motif of the terpene cyclase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 7. Gene disruption construct of efuA and mutant veriﬁcation.A. Scheme of the gene knock-out construct and PCR ampliﬁed regions for
mutant veriﬁcation (Ct1 and Ct2: control PCR1 and 2).B. PCR detection of positive Δ efuA disruption mutants. L, 1 kb ladder; 1, wild type Ct1;
2, wild-type Ct2; 3, mutant Ct1; 4, mutant Ct2.C. Growth of wild-type (WT) and mutant (ΔefuA) on SMY media without (−Hyg) or supplemented
with hygromycin (+Hyg). (Note: the wild-type proliferates mainly in the hyaline yeast-like stage on unamended medium, whereas the mutant
grows mainly as ﬁlamentous melanized hyphae in the hygromycin-amended medium). [Colour ﬁgure can be viewed at wileyonlinelibrary.com]

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 8. Veriﬁcation of enfumafungin production in wild-type and mutant strains of H. carpetanum.A. Comparison of HPLC-UV chromatograms
derived from wild-type (red line) and ΔefuA mutant (green line) extracts. The enfumafungin standard is depicted in blue (Note: under regular
HPLC conditions enfumafungin appears in two conformations yielding two overlapping peaks).B. Agar-well-diffusion assays of wild-type and
mutant extracts against C. albicans (1–3: wild-type, 4–6: ΔefuA mutant, 7: 70 μM enfumafungin, 8: 54 μM amphotericin B, 9: methanol). [Colour
ﬁgure can be viewed at wileyonlinelibrary.com]
